主要内容: California regulators approved a historic plan to mandate rooftop solar panels on most new single-family homes and multi-family residential buildings up to three stories, starting in 2020. The mandate is expected to add about $9,500 to the cost of building new houses but is projected to be offset by long-term energy savings. The decision, approved 5-to-0 by the California Energy Commission, is part of the state's 2019 update of energy efficiency standards and ongoing efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The state's building sector is the second-largest source of greenhouse gas emissions when fossil fuels are factored in. The move has sent solar industry stocks higher, with SunPower, Sunrun, First Solar, and Tesla seeing gains of 6%, 4%, 3%, and nearly 2%, respectively. The policy also applies to ventilation systems and indoor air quality, with the ultimate goal of achieving net-zero energy homes that reduce carbon footprints and make buildings energy self-sufficient. Some experts warn that increasing construction costs may worsen the state's affordable housing crisis.
